stem:
Match the species in Column I with their classification in Column II.

Column I:
P. Cyclopentadienyl anion
Q. Cyclopentadienyl cation
R. Cyclopropenyl cation
S. Cyclopropenyl radical

Column II:
1. Aromatic (6 pi electrons)
2. Anti-aromatic (4 pi electrons)
3. Aromatic (2 pi electrons)
4. Non-aromatic (3 pi electrons)

Choose the correct matching set.

verdicts.working: P has 6 π electrons and is aromatic; Q has 4 and is anti-aromatic; R has 2 and is aromatic; S has 3 and is non-aromatic. Hence P-1, Q-2, R-3, S-4.

working:
Cyclopentadienyl anion has 6 pi electrons (4n+2, n=1) and is aromatic. Cyclopentadienyl cation has 4 pi electrons and is anti-aromatic. Cyclopropenyl cation has 2 pi electrons (4n+2, n=0) and is aromatic. Cyclopropenyl radical has 3 pi electrons and is non-aromatic. Hence P-1, Q-2, R-3, S-4.

Independent check: P has 6 π electrons and is aromatic; Q has 4 and is anti-aromatic; R has 2 and is aromatic; S has 3 and is non-aromatic. Hence P-1, Q-2, R-3, S-4.
solution:
By Hückel’s rule, a planar cyclic conjugated system is aromatic with $4n+2$ π electrons and anti-aromatic with $4n$ π electrons.
Cyclopentadienyl anion has $6$ π electrons (aromatic), while the cation has $4$ (anti-aromatic).
Cyclopropenyl cation has $2$ π electrons (aromatic); the radical has $3$ π electrons and is non-aromatic.
Hence, $P$–1, $Q$–2, $R$–3, $S$–4.
